sh: Inflation climbs in euro area and UK
headline: Inflation rises to 4.0% in the euro area and 3.6% in the UK, driven by energy
summary: Eurostat confirmed on Wednesday 18 November that euro area inflation rose to 4.0% in October, up from 3.8% in September. UK inflation rose to 3.6% from 3.5%, the Office for National Statistics said the same day.
why: When prices rise faster, household budgets are squeezed and central banks are less likely to cut interest rates. Energy prices are the main driver in both the euro area and the UK.

event.t: Euro area annual inflation was 4.0% in October, up from 3.8% in September and 2.1% a year earlier, Eurostat said.
In Eurostat’s first estimate, energy prices were 20.8% higher than a year earlier, the biggest driver. Services prices rose 3.3%.

In the UK, consumer prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5%, the Office for National Statistics said. Fuel prices were again a major cause. Core inflation, which leaves out energy and food, was 2.8%.
The European Commission expects euro area inflation to peak above 4% between late 2026 and early 2027 and then ease, it said in its autumn forecast on 17 November.

effects.label: Households
effects.t: Prices are rising faster, which squeezes budgets.

effects.label: Interest rates
effects.t: Higher inflation makes rate cuts by the European Central Bank and the Bank of England less likely.
